pool.text: A violent confrontation occurred between local Yidinji people and Phillip Garland over well usage.
The city was founded and named following the discovery of gold in the river.
The Cairns Parish of the Roman Catholic Vicariate Apostolic of Cooktown was established.
Chinese population accounted for sixty percent of all farmers and ninety percent of gardeners.
The Wharf Estate Cairns went on sale in Brisbane via auction by John Macnamara.
The creation of a harbour board supported the robust economic future of the port.
The Cairns Sailors and Soldiers War Memorial was unveiled by Alexander Frederick Draper.
Combat missions were flown out of Cairns in support of the coral sea battle.
The City of Cairns Open professional golf tournament was inaugurated.
The Cairns and District Chinese Association was established as an arts and heritage organisation.
The City Library, operated by the Cairns Regional Council, opened at Abbott Street.
The opening of the Cairns International Airport established the city as a desirable destination.
The controversial private road named Quaid Road was constructed through a heritage area.
The Cairns and District Family History Society maintains a library of genealogy material.
A major refurbishment was undertaken at the City Library operated by the regional council.
The Northern Pride Queensland Cup rugby league team played their first season.
The Queensland Government opened the second stage of William McCormack Place office building.
The Cairns City bus station opened as one of the main bus hubs.
A new building was completed to provide up to one hundred sixty-eight more beds.
Far North Queensland Heat soccer team played until their dissolution in this year.
